subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by making CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with no direct WAL maintenance while a gateway lease is active, by enforcing a broader single-writer shared-state lease, or by prioritizing malformed-DB quarantine/recovery first?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the permanent behavior changes CLI observability, doctor/state migrations, gateway ownership, and recovery policy for a persisted shared store.

options.title: RPC-first no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Health/status/stability should prefer the live gateway and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file fallback while a gateway lease is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: The gateway should own writer-style and WAL-maintenance access, and other processes should refuse shared-state DB opens that could mutate while the lease is held.

options.title: Recovery/quarantine first
options.body: OpenClaw should first preserve and quarantine malformed `openclaw.sqlite` stores, then address direct CLI/gateway concurrent maintenance as a follow-up.

recommendation.title: RPC-first no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Health/status/stability should prefer the live gateway and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file fallback while a gateway lease is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared SQLite state database introduction is the strongest available ownership signal for choosing the DB ownership and recovery contract.
